target_audience: High School, College, and University Students
title_idea: Alpha vs Sigma: The Student Psychology Breakdown
core_psychological_thesis: The Alpha derives his power from the hierarchy and dies without external validation. The Sigma exists outside the hierarchy and derives his power from total self-reliance. On campus, the Alpha performs for the crowd, while the Sigma owns his life in silence.

alpha_student.psychological_definition: External status seeker. Needs a pack to lead and an audience to validate him. Fragile ego masked by loud gestures, brand flexing, and constant dominance displays.
alpha_student.campus_behavior: Walks with an entourage, shouts in the hallway, demands to be group project leader, panics when ignored.

sigma_student.psychological_definition: Autonomous sovereign. Exists completely outside the social hierarchy. Highly competent, socially immune, emotionally detached, comfortable alone.
sigma_student.campus_behavior: Sits in the back corner with coffee, doesn't participate in shallow drama, studies high-leverage skills, unbothered by rejection.

narrative_arc.shot_1: The Definition: What Alpha and Sigma actually mean (External Hierarchy vs Internal Sovereignty).
narrative_arc.shot_2: The Classroom Test: Group project and lecture dynamics (Loud showoff vs Quiet master).
narrative_arc.shot_3: The Hallway & Canteen: Social flexing with entourage vs Eating alone comfortably.
narrative_arc.shot_4: Handling Disrespect: Alpha explosive ego rage vs Sigma unbothered cold stare.
narrative_arc.shot_5: The Girl / Dating Dynamic: Desperate peacocking vs Natural magnetic gravity.
narrative_arc.shot_6: The Graduation Paradox: Validation burnout vs Silent empire building.
